findings.title: A project's own skills are also stored under the machine-wide key, so they leak into other projects' lists
findings.body:
The header comment (lines 5-6) says a project's own skills belong to that project's tasks only. But `rememberChatSkills` calls `remember(keyFor(hostId, harness), skills)` (line 25) on every report, including a chat that belongs to a project. That chat's list may hold project-scoped skills. `rememberedChatSkills` falls back to that same key (line 31) for any other project, and for a standalone task where `projectId` is undefined. So after you open a chat in project A, a New task in project B or in Standalone lists A's project-only skills first. `mergeChatSkills` keeps the reported list in front, so they can't be filtered out later. Choosing one inserts a `/skill` the agent doesn't have there.

The test at rememberedSkills.test.ts:9-17 misses this. The project-less report on line 11 overwrites the generic key, so it never checks that p1's `ship` stays out of p2. Write the machine-wide key only from a chat with no project, or from skills that aren't project-scoped. Then add a test that reports `[compact, ship]` for p1 only and expects `rememberedChatSkills("h1","claude-code","p2")` to be empty or to hold no `ship`.

findings.title: A failed refresh replaces an already loaded list with an empty one, and the panel can't tell the two apart
findings.body: The comment at lines 208-209 says the list for this loader "stays up as it is read again". The `.catch` on line 220 does the opposite: it stores `skills: []` for the same loader. A transient failure on reopen therefore replaces a good list, and the panel shows the empty state (empty `items` with an empty query still renders). That is the same state as "the machine offers none". `loadSpawnSkills` only rethrows when a chat has reported no skills, so only that case ends here. Consider keeping the previous `loaded` entry on error and recording the failure separately, so the panel doesn't present an unreachable machine as an empty one.

findings.title: Two comments are interleaved above `loadSkills`
findings.body: The comment on lines 701-703 describes the skill loader. The comment and state on lines 704-705 are about the overlay, and they sit between that comment and `loadSkills` on lines 708-712. Move the overlay state and its comment above the loader comment, or put the loader comment directly on `loadSkills`.

findings.title: `getAgentSkills` takes no abort signal, unlike the neighbouring `getAgentModels` calls
findings.body: In `spawn.tsx` the `getAgentModels` calls pass `polling.signal` (lines 634 and 688). The skills request has no signal and no timeout of its own beyond `req`'s defaults. A request in flight when the user leaves the page or changes machine finishes in the background. `requestGate` stops it from publishing, but the request itself isn't cancelled. This is low impact, since the 30s cache shares the in-flight promise, so it is not a defect.

contracts.action: New "/" skill list on the New task composer, loaded when the list opens
contracts.equivalent_path: The chat composer's "/" list (ChatComposer) uses `conversation.skills`, which the agent session reports.
contracts.before_after: The new path reads the list via `onLoadSkills`, which calls `loadSpawnSkills`. That function merges the remembered chat list with the scan from `GET /agents/:id/skills`. Each open of the list starts a request, guarded by `requestGate`. The gate is invalidated on close and on unmount, and `loaded` is tied to the loader identity, so another agent's or project's list isn't shown.
contracts.visible_effect: `onLoadSkills` is undefined on Cloud, so there is no list. The panel then goes to the page's overlay host, or into the composer's own column when there is no host.
contracts.failure_mode: A network error with no remembered chat list shows an empty panel, which looks the same as "no skills". A 404 from an older daemon gives an empty list that stays cached for 30s. The error is not cached, so the next open retries.

contracts.action: Remember a chat's reported skills for the New task page, and drop them when a machine is forgotten
contracts.equivalent_path: `rememberedTurnOptions`, which is likewise cleared in `forgetPairedHost` and `forgetServer`.
contracts.before_after: An effect stores `conversation.skills` under host, harness and project, and writes the machine-wide key as well. The two `forgetRememberedChatSkills()` calls in disconnect.ts clear it, but the 30s `spawnSkills` cache is not cleared.
contracts.visible_effect: The New task list starts from the skills a chat of the same agent last reported. Project-scoped skills also appear in other projects' lists, because of the machine-wide key.
contracts.failure_mode: Nothing is lost on failure. The list is wrong in the cross-project case (reported as a finding).

summary: The "/" skill list on the New task page is mostly sound. Loading is guarded against stale and out-of-order results. The overlay-host wiring cleans up on unmount, and Cloud is excluded. One real defect: `rememberChatSkills` also writes a project chat's list under the machine-wide key, so a project's own skills show up in other projects' and standalone lists. This contradicts the file's own comment, and the test doesn't catch it. Smaller points: a failed refresh turns an already-loaded list into an empty one, two comments are interleaved in spawn.tsx, and the skills request has no abort signal. I did not build or run anything.
